tutorial.title: Using the Filters Dictionary
tutorial.descriptionContent: Using the filters dictionary to write specific queries.
tutorial.shortDescriptionContent: Python learners who know GET requests and single filters

lessons.title: Separate the request details
lessons.interactiveContent:
We've seen how to use query parameters directly in the URL.

Now, we'll explore a dedicated filter dictionary to help us keep request details separate from the URL and make them easier to work with.

lessons.title: Store the parameter - Copy
lessons.interactiveContent:
We use a dictionary to define the filter that we previously defined in the query parameter.

Create an empty dictionary called filters.

Make sure to pick filters followed by = and then {, }.
lessons.hardModeContent:
We use a dictionary to define the filter that we previously defined in the query parameter.

Create an empty dictionary called filters.

Make sure to pick filters, followed by =, {, and finally }.

lessons.title: Store the parameter
lessons.interactiveContent:
A dictionary key becomes the parameter name.

Add a key named id with value 1, since we want to filter for the course with ID 1.

Make sure to pick "id", followed by :, and finally 1.

lessons.title: Build the dictionary
lessons.interactiveContent:
A dictionary value becomes the parameter value.

Set it to 2 to filter for elements with the ID 2.

Make sure to type 2.

lessons.title: Use the params argument
lessons.interactiveContent:
The params argument tells requests.get() where query parameters belong.

Add the argument with an empty dictionary. You'll pass the saved filters next.

Make sure to pick params followed by = and then {, }.

lessons.title: Pass the filters
lessons.interactiveContent:
We pass the filters dictionary as the value of params if we want the get() function to use it.

requests builds the query string and sends the customized GET request using query parameters: https://mimo.org/courses?id=2.

Make sure to pick filters, followed by params=, and finally filters.
lessons.hardModeContent:
We pass the filters dictionary as the value of params if we want the get() function to use it.

The requests library builds the query string from this dictionary and sends the customized GET request.

Fetch course ID 2 using the saved query filters.

Make sure to pick "id", followed by 2, get, params, and finally filters.

lessons.title: Reusable Multiple Filters
lessons.interactiveContent:
We know how to filter by a single value using a filter dictionary.

Just like with query parameters in a URL, we can combine multiple filters in the same dictionary.

lessons.title: Set the First Filter
lessons.interactiveContent:
Let's start by building a dictionary with a single entry for filtering.

Make sure to pick filters followed by = and then {, "language": "python", }.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Create filters and store one entry that filters for Python courses using the language key.

Make sure to pick filters, followed by =, {, "language": "python", and finally }.

lessons.title: Add Another Entry
lessons.interactiveContent:
Since a filter dictionary is just a Python dictionary, we can add multiple values, separating them with commas.

Add "level": "beginner" as the second entry.

Make sure to pick ,, followed by "level":, and finally "beginner".
lessons.hardModeContent:
Since a filter dictionary is just a Python dictionary, we can add multiple values, separating them with commas.

Keep Python as the language and add a level filter for beginner courses.

Make sure to pick "python", followed by ,, "level", :, and finally "beginner".

lessons.title: Pass the Filters
lessons.interactiveContent:
Once we have the dictionary ready, we pass it as the params argument, which converts each dictionary entry into a query parameter.

Pass filters as params=filters.

Make sure to pick params, followed by =, and finally filters.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Once we have the dictionary ready, we pass it as the params argument, which converts each dictionary entry into a query parameter.

Request beginner Python courses using the dictionary as query parameters.

Make sure to pick "python", followed by "beginner", params, =, and finally filters.

lessons.title: Receive the Response
lessons.interactiveContent:
The get() call returns a response after applying both course filters, and the response contains courses that match every dictionary entry.

Store the returned response in response and print it.

Make sure to pick response followed by data and then response.json(), data.
lessons.hardModeContent:
The get() call returns a response after applying both course filters, and the response contains courses that match every dictionary entry.

Store the request result in response. Parse it into data and print that data.

Make sure to pick params, followed by filters, response, json, and finally data.
